newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Orogen cannot explain share surge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Orogen cannot explain share surge.

text.p: Papua New Guinea resources investor Orogen Minerals Ltd said it did not have any information for release to the market which could explain the recent surge in its share price other than point to information about its PNG oil exploration activities and recent share issue.

Orogen, which is 51 percent-owned by the PNG government and which owns that country's mineral resources development division, told the Australian Stock Exchange that it was a partner in the prospective Moran 1X sidetrack well.
Brokers said on Wednesday that the rise in Orogen and Oil Search Ltd was due to the Moran results.

The stock exchange had asked Orogen if it had any information which could explain the rise in its share price to A$2.49 on Wednesday from A$2.13 on November 6. Moran's drilling partners said on Tuesday the well had two hydrocarbon shows.
Orogen shares listed on November 1, with the stock opening at A$2.05 compared with the A$2.00 issue price to institutions.
The offer was oversubscribed by up to 10 to 15 times and Orogen told the stock exchange that continued demand for its stock could also be pushing the share price higher.
